main_body: A T-shaped timber post: a horizontal crossbeam at the top (rows 9-17) on a thin vertical pole (rows 18-47).
top_band: Crossbeam rows 10-12 in orange (L=157), then a cream highlight row 13 (L=239). This is only a 3-row light band over the beam's front face, with no depth. The beam reads as a flat front-facing plank.
evidence: The crossbeam is 9 rows tall: orange rows 10-12, cream edge row 13, then brownish rows 14-15 and an outline. That gives about 3 light rows over about 2 front rows, so it could pass as a thin top surface. But the pole below is a 3-4px wide vertical strip drawn straight on with no top face and no base. The post is a flat elevation with no horizontal surface visible, and the pole has no visible foot. The beam top is too shallow and sits directly over a flat-shaded pole. Under strict reading, the main body (the pole, the largest volume) is in front elevation, so the whole drawing fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours and 0 median colours per full tile (it is smaller than a tile in width), against 38-40 colours in the references. The pole is a nearly flat 2-3 tone strip with a thin outline, and the crossbeam has only a few dots of variation. The outline is a tinted dark brown, not neutral black (0% neutral), which is good. Even so, it is much thinner and simpler than the stall and well references.
